lines.text: Detective. Visiting hours for the living are short, so be efficient. You’re here about a ten-year-old death, not about Mr. Ishida. I can tell from your face.

...You brought that file in here. Then you should know I was a trainee at this office that June, Detective, and I assisted at her autopsy. I recorded grip bruises on both wrists — adult fingers — and sedatives in her blood with no prescription anywhere. My supervisor called the bruises 'from the fall' and signed it an accident. I kept my own notes. I have never shown them to anyone, until possibly now.

Your notes are incomplete, Detective — deliberately, on my part. All four wounds came from the same blade: short, thin, single-edged, kept razor sharp. A kitchen petty knife. The cuts are economical — the work of someone who cuts things every day for a living. I left that out of the reports as 'speculation.' It still is. But cooks, surgeons, florists — someone's hands have been doing this motion for years.
